_meta.subject: Small powerboat (5-6 m, ~100-115 hp outboard, ~GBP 40,000 / CAD 68,000) kept by a Londoner in the UK or by a Toronto-area resident in Ontario
_meta.conventions: sourceType is 'primary' when the insurer's, marina's or maker's own page or document is the source, else 'secondary'. confirmed=true means the figure was read directly from the fetched page or PDF on 2026-09-30; false means it came only from a search-engine snippet, or it is a derivation. Nothing here was invented: where no figure is published the value is null with a note. Derived figures are labeled 'derived' and show their arithmetic.
_meta.currencyNotes: UK figures are GBP including 20% VAT unless noted. Ontario figures are CAD and exclude 13% HST unless noted.

uk.item: Typical annual yacht premium as a share of agreed hull value
uk.note: Range attributed to London Marine Insurance Services Ltd (a Lloyd's placing broker), quoted by a US cruising blog. The same article says most cruising yachts fall between 1% and 5%, with a typical owner near 1.5%. Not a UK insurer's own page.
uk.publisher: The Boat Galley (quoting London Marine Insurance Services Ltd)

uk.item: UK motorboat insurance, published range and the broker's average
uk.note: The broker labels these indicative UK estimates for 2026, not guaranteed premiums. Its GBP 225 average is across all motorboats it insures, most smaller or cheaper than GBP 40,000, so it is not a figure for this boat. The page gives no percentage of value.

No premium or rate is published; the page says premiums are tailored and sends readers to a quote. The only price shown is the Marine Legal Protection add-on, GBP 15.00 plus Insurance Premium Tax per year.

uncertain: UK insurance: no named UK insurer (Navigators & General, Haven Knox-Johnston, GJW Direct, Bishop Skinner) publishes an example premium or a percentage-of-value rate. The 1-1.5% figure is a Lloyd's broker's range quoted second-hand; GBP 400-600 for a GBP 40,000 boat is derived.

Ontario insurance: Erie Mutual's 1.5% rule gives CAD 1,020 for a CAD 68,000 boat, but a broker's bands put mid-size powerboats at CAD 500-800. Intact, Aviva Canada and Skippers' Plan publish no averages.

Toronto minimums: Outer Harbour charges a 30 ft minimum, so an 18 ft boat pays for 30 ft. Bluffer's Park prints no minimum for slips, only a 20 ft minimum for trailer-with-ramp. Port Credit Harbour Marina and Ashbridges Bay Yacht Club publish no rate sheets.
No Toronto marina publishes a fuel price. The nearest published Lake Ontario figure is Cobourg (CAD 2.45/L gas, 2026-09-25), from a marina-reported aggregator.
Mercury/Princecraft: no fuel-burn figure for a Mercury 90 or 115 on a Princecraft Sport 175 could be read. Mercury's performance database blocked automated access and Boating's table is an image.

Honda BF100 on the Cap Camarat 5.5 CC: not found. Jeanneau's own file tests Yamaha F100 and F115 only. The Honda figure (3.72 gph = 14.1 L/h at 4000 rpm, 23.3 mph) comes from a 5.4 m Highfield RIB, which is lighter than the 1.3 t Cap Camarat. The Yamaha F100 on the Cap Camarat burned 15.6 L/h at 4000 rpm, 19.3 kn.
Hamble Point trailer storage: the July 2026 tariff reads GBP 386.55 per metre per year (up to 5.9 m), not the GBP 372 given as known.
London to Hamble travel time comes from a train-booking site, not the rail operator.
